Judgment:

entities.text:

Others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: This appeal is preferred by the appellants being aggrieved by the judgment and decree dated 15.04.2003 passed in O.P.No.654 of 1999 by the Principal Motor Vehicle Accidents Claims Tribunal (Principal District Court) at Warangal (for short 'the Tribunal), whereby the Tribunal has granted an amount of Rs.1,56,000/- towards compensation as against the claim of Rs.4,00,000/-.

entities.text: Principal Motor Vehicle Accidents Claims Tribunal (Principal District Court) at Warangal
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 2. The manner in which the accident had taken place and the liability is not disputed.

However, the learned counsel appearing for the appellants would submit that though a claim was made that the deceased was earning an amount of Rs.3,000/- per month from doing agriculture and labour work and also having Acs.4.00 gts. of land, the Tribunal committed an error in refusing to consider the said income of the deceased only on the ground that the documents were not filed to that effect.
3.

On the other hand, the learned Standing Counsel appearing for the Insurance Company would submit that the accident occurred in the year 1998 and at that relevant point of time, the labourer was earning around Rs.1,000/- per month.
4. It is not disputed that the deceased was working as a labourer.

During the relevant point i.e.,
1998, the daily wage would have been Rs.100/- per day and considering that the deceased would have worked for twenty five days, this Court deems it appropriate to consider the income of the deceased at Rs.2,500/- per month.
5. Insofar as the deduction towards personal and living expenses is concerned, the deceased was married and survived by wife and two children, then total dependents are three.

As per the decision of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Sarla Verma and others v. Delhi Transport Corporation and another 1, the standard deduction towards personal and living expenses of the deceased should be one-third.

entities.text: Sarla Verma and others v. Delhi Transport Corporation and another 1
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In National Insurance Company Limited v. Pranay Sethi and others 2, the Hon'ble Apex Court at paragraph 59.4 held that in case the deceased was self-employed, an addition of 40% of the income should be awarded towards future prospects, where the deceased age was below 40 years.

entities.text: National Insurance Company Limited v. Pranay Sethi and others 2
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Since the age of the deceased at the time of the accident was 32 years, 40% of monthly income of the deceased can be taken towards future prospects.

sentences.text: With regard to the multiplier, as per the decision of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Sarla Verma (1 supra), the multiplier is '16' for the age groups of 31 to 35.
The age of the deceased as on the date of the accident was 32 years.

8. The Hon'ble Supreme Court in Anjali and others v. Lokendra Rathod and others 3, decided on 06.12.2022, taking into consideration the decision of Sarala Verma (supra) and also the case of Pranay Sethi (supra) and also taking into consideration the rise in expenditure and cost of (2017) 16 SCC 680 2023(1) ALD 107(SC) living, has awarded a sum of Rs.44,000/- towards loss of consortium.

entities.text: Anjali and others v. Lokendra Rathod and others 3
entities.label: PRECEDENT

At this stage, learned Standing Counsel for the Insurance Company submits that the claimants claimed only a sum of Rs.4,00,000/- as compensation and the quantum of compensation which is now awarded would go beyond the claim made which is impermissible under law.

In view of the judgments of the Hon'ble Apex Court in Laxman @ Laxman Mourya v. Divisional Manager, Oriental Insurance Company Limited and another 4 and in Nagappa v. Gurudayal Singh 5, the claimants are entitled to get more amount than what has been claimed.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

2 extent.

sentences.text: In the result, the appeal is allowed enhancing the compensation amount awarded by the Tribunal from Rs.1,56,000/- to Rs.6,10,000/-.
The enhanced amount shall be deposited by respondent Nos.1 to 3 jointly and severally within a period of two (2) months from the date of receipt of a copy of this judgment.
The enhanced compensation amount shall carry interest @ 7.5% per annum from the date of claim petition till (2011) 10 SCC 756 2003 ACJ 12 (SC) realization.
The claimants are entitled to the apportionment of the amount as directed by the Tribunal.
On such deposit, the claimants are permitted to withdraw the amount without furnishing any security.
However, the claimants are directed to deposit the deficit Court fee on the enhanced amount.
There shall be no order as to costs.
Miscellaneous petitions pending, if any, shall stand closed.
